2609.01369.title: How Correct Is Your Answer? A Semantic Correctness Framework for Open QA Evaluation
2609.01369.paper_summary: Reliable evaluation of open-ended question answering remains a bottleneck for measuring answer correctness of modern LLMs. Unlike multiple-choice tasks, free-form answers may be correct in many surface forms and may fail in qualitatively different ways, including incompleteness, contradiction, overgeneration, and endorsement of false premises. Existing judgment-based and similarity-based metrics often collapse these distinctions. We address this gap with three reusable contributions. First, we introduce a semantic correctness taxonomy that assigns open-ended answers to eight ordered classes, separating verbose-but-correct answers from those contaminated by hallucinated content. Second, we release CAP-Correctness, an 8.8k-example benchmark spanning widely used QA datasets, and CAP-Statements, an 11k-example dataset for converting question-answer pairs into declarative statements for natural language inference (NLI) training and statement-based evaluation. Third, we introduce CAP (Context-Aware Precision), a reference-based metric that scores question-conditioned statements using bidirectional NLI. Under a monotonicity protocol testing whether metrics respect the taxonomy's intended ordering, CAP outperforms established baselines.
2609.01369.paper_summary_zh: 可靠的開放式問題回答評估仍然是衡量現代大型語言模型（LLMs）答案正確性的瓶頸。與多選任務不同，自由形式的答案可能以多種表面形式正確，並可能以質量不同的方式失敗，包括不完整、矛盾、過度生成和支持錯誤前提。現有的基於判斷和相似度的度量通常會模糊這些區別。我們通過三個可重用的貢獻來解決這一問題。首先，我們引入了一個語義正確性分類法，將開放式答案分配到八個有序類別中，將冗長但正確的答案與受到幻覺內容污染的答案分開。其次，我們發布了CAP-Correctness，一個包含8.8k示例的基準，涵蓋廣泛使用的問答數據集，以及CAP-Statements，一個包含11k示例的數據集，用於將問題-答案對轉換為自然語言推理（NLI）訓練和基於陳述的評估。第三，我們引入了CAP（上下文感知精度），這是一種基於參考的度量，使用雙向NLI對問題條件語句進行打分。在測試度量是否遵循分類法預期排序的單調性協議下，CAP的表現超過了既定基準。
